title: Walking, cycling, and sharing rides
description: Short journeys are where transport money and emissions quietly pile up — and where change is easiest.

body.heading: The short-journey habit
paragraphs: A large share of car journeys are surprisingly short — distances that are walkable or cyclable in 10–20 minutes. Swapping even some of them saves fuel, parking costs, and wear, while adding movement to your day.
Start with one regular journey: the school run, the station, the local shop. One swapped trip, repeated weekly, becomes a habit with real totals by the end of a year.

body.heading: Sharing the rest
paragraphs: For journeys that need a vehicle, sharing lifts with friends, neighbours, or colleagues splits costs and emissions. Public transport turns travel time into reading or rest time, which has its own value.
If you cycle, basic maintenance — pumped tyres, working brakes, a little chain oil — keeps it safe and pleasant, and a second-hand bike in good condition is one of the cheapest vehicles there is.

body.heading: Safety and realism
paragraphs: Choose routes you feel safe on, be visible in the dark, and skip the swap in dangerous weather. A sustainable habit is one that still feels sensible in February.

takeaway: Swap one regular short journey to walking or cycling, and share the rides that remain.
